<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">
<script>try{var k="np-theme",v=localStorage.getItem(k);
if(!localStorage.getItem("np-theme-v2")){if(v==="light"){localStorage.removeItem(k);v=null}localStorage.setItem("np-theme-v2","1")}
document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme",v||"dark")}catch(e){}
/* A skipped cross-document view transition rejects a promise no author code
   owns. It can fire before any deferred script has run, so the listener has to
   be registered here rather than in app.js. Matched narrowly: everything else,
   including unrelated AbortErrors, still reaches the console. */
addEventListener("unhandledrejection",function(e){var r=e.reason;if(r&&r.name==="AbortError"&&/transition was skipped/i.test(r.message||""))e.preventDefault()});</script>

attention-lab.html.title: Attention Lab · KnowML
attention-lab.html.description: Step through Multi-Head Attention, KV caching, MQA, GQA, Multi-Head Latent Attention, PagedAttention and FlashAttention on one small worked example — every matrix, every shape, every number computed live and checkable by hand.

backprop-lab.html.title: Backprop Lab · KnowML
backprop-lab.html.description: Backpropagation through a 3→4→2 network, computed live: the forward pass, the chain rule backward one derivative at a time, every gradient checked against central differences, and one step of descent that actually lowers the loss.

index.html.title: KnowML — Learn modern AI, watch it run, then ship it
index.html.description: Everything around modern AI in one place: 37 sections from linear algebra to agents, five interactive labs where every number is computed live, four learning roadmaps, a model atlas, and 286 interview questions to drill.
index.html.notesPlaceholder: Jot down anything — your own study plan, gaps to revisit…

labs.html.title: The Labs · KnowML
labs.html.description: Five interactive labs that step through attention, backpropagation, byte-pair encoding, quantization and sampling one operation at a time. Every matrix on screen is computed in your browser, never typed in.

map.html.title: Site Map · KnowML
map.html.description: Every page on KnowML as one navigable graph — 42 destinations grouped by theme, with the labs attached to the topics they belong to.

practice.html.title: Where to Practice · KnowML
practice.html.description: Reading will not make you good at machine learning. Where to actually practise — Deep-ML for drills, Kaggle and ML Contests for judgement under a real metric, Karpathy and ARENA for building from scratch — and which one fixes the gap you actually have.

quantization-lab.html.title: Quantization Lab · KnowML
quantization-lab.html.description: Quantize one small weight matrix to INT8 and INT4 and watch exactly what is lost — scales, integer codes, dequantized weights and the error matrix, all computed live, plus the outlier that wastes 87% of the integer range and the per-channel fix that recovers it.

review.html.title: Review · KnowML
review.html.description: Drill the interview questions from every section with spaced repetition — answer, rate yourself, and let the schedule bring each one back exactly when you are about to forget it.

roadmaps.html.title: Learning Roadmaps · KnowML
roadmaps.html.description: Four ordered routes through the 37 topic pages: total beginner to training a model, classical ML to reading a transformer paper, understanding LLMs to shipping one, and a dense interview path. Each stage has a checkpoint you can actually perform, an honest time estimate, and a list of what to skip.

<style>
/* Scoped to this page only. Everything here is namespaced under .rm-page or
   .rm-*, so nothing can leak into a topic page. If any of this ever becomes
   useful twice, it should move into style.css instead of being copied. */
/* .layout.home zeroes the content padding (three classes of specificity), which
   is right for the homepage hero and wrong for a page of prose. Beat it. */
.layout.home .content.rm-page { max-width: 980px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 40px 32px 100px; }
@media (max-width: 700px) { .layout.home .content.rm-page { padding: 26px 18px 80px; } }
/* one stage of one roadmap: a rail down the left so the reading list, the
   checkpoint and the skip list read as one unit rather than three */
.rm-page .rm-stage { border-left: 2px solid var(--border-soft); padding-left: 22px; margin: 0 0 34px; }
.rm-page .rm-stage:last-of-type { margin-bottom: 22px; }
.rm-page .rm-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-bottom: 12px; }
.rm-page .rm-num {
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .07em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent-text); flex-shrink: 0;
}
.rm-page .rm-title { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -.01em; color: var(--text); }
/* Outside a track this sat hard right, which read fine on a full-width prose
   block. Inside the map it left the estimate stranded half a screen from the
   title it belongs to, so it now follows the title directly. */
.rm-page .rm-time {
  margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 11.5px;
  color: var(--text-faint); flex-shrink: 0;
}
.rm-page .rm-track .rm-time { margin-left: 0; }
.rm-page .rm-stage .order-strip { margin-bottom: 14px; }
.rm-page .rm-stage p { font-size: 17px; margin-bottom: 16px; }
/* Four chooser cards in the shared auto-fill grid land 3 + 1, which leaves a
   hole the width of two cards. Two abreast pairs them evenly instead. */
.rm-page .rm-chooser { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
@media (max-width: 700px) { .rm-page .rm-chooser { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
/* ---------- the map ----------
   One node per stage on a rail. The rail is a pseudo-element on .rm-map rather
   than a drawn SVG so it stretches with the flex row at any node count, and
   wraps to a vertical stack on narrow screens without a second layout. */
.rm-page .rm-track { margin: 0 0 20px; }
.rm-page .rm-map {
  position: relative; display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: flex-start;
  padding: 26px 4px 12px; margin-bottom: 6px;
}
/* One segment per gap, drawn on each node after the first, spanning from the
   previous node's centre to this one. A single bar with percentage insets can
   only be right for one node count, and the tracks have four and five. */
.rm-page .rm-hint-tap { display: none; }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap { position: relative; flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap + .rm-node-wrap::before {
  content: ''; position: absolute; top: 45px; height: 2px;
  left: calc(-50% - 10px); width: calc(100% + 10px);   /* 10px = the flex gap */
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 42%, transparent);
  pointer-events: none;
}
.rm-page .rm-node {
  position: relative; z-index: 1;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 9px;
  width: 100%; padding: 4px 6px 8px;
  background: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; font: inherit; text-align: center;
  color: var(--text-dim);
  transition: color .2s var(--ease), transform .2s var(--ease);
}
.rm-page .rm-dot {
  display: grid; place-items: center;
  width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 50%;
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700;
  /* The --c-* palette is built for swatches on a dark card. As text on the
     light page these measured 2.72:1; mixing half the track colour into the
     body text colour self-corrects per theme — 6.28:1 light, 9.44:1 dark —
     and keeps the hue. Same ratio the door cards on the homepage use. */
  color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 50%, var(--text));
  background: var(--bg);
  border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 70%, var(--bg));
  transition: background-color .2s var(--ease), border-color .2s var(--ease),
              box-shadow .2s var(--ease), color .2s var(--ease);
}
.rm-page .rm-node-label {
  font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; letter-spacing: -.005em;
}
.rm-page .rm-node-help {
  position: absolute; top: 2px; right: calc(50% - 30px);
  width: 15px; height: 15px; border-radius: 50%;
  display: grid; place-items: center;
  font-size: 10px; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1;
  color: var(--bg); background: var(--text-faint);
  opacity: 0; transform: scale(.6);
  transition: opacity .18s var(--ease), transform .18s var(--ease), background-color .18s var(--ease);
}
.rm-page .rm-node:hover, .rm-page .rm-node:focus-visible { color: var(--text); outline: none; }
.rm-page .rm-node:hover .rm-dot, .rm-page .rm-node:focus-visible .rm-dot {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 16%, var(--bg));
  border-color: var(--track, var(--accent));
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 16%, transparent);
}
.rm-page .rm-node:hover .rm-node-help, .rm-page .rm-node:focus-visible .rm-node-help {
  opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); background: var(--track, var(--accent));
}
.rm-page .rm-node.is-active .rm-dot {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 50%, var(--text));
  color: var(--bg);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 50%, var(--text));
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 20%, transparent);
}
.rm-page .rm-node.is-active { color: var(--text); }
/* ---------- the hover card ----------
   Anchored to the node and centred on it, except at the ends of the rail where
   centring would push it off the page — the first and last cards align to their
   own edge instead. */
.rm-page .rm-pop {
  position: absolute; top: calc(100% - 2px); left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%) translateY(4px);
  z-index: 20; width: 252px; max-width: 70vw;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px;
  padding: 13px 15px; text-align: left;
  background: var(--bg-card); border: 1px solid var(--border-hover);
  border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg);
  opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; pointer-events: none;
  transition: opacity .18s var(--ease), transform .18s var(--ease), visibility .18s;
}
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:first-child .rm-pop { left: 0; transform: translateX(0) translateY(4px); }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:last-child  .rm-pop { left: auto; right: 0; transform: translateX(0) translateY(4px); }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:hover .rm-pop,
.rm-page .rm-node:focus-visible ~ .rm-pop { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; transform: translateX(-50%) translateY(0); }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:first-child:hover .rm-pop,
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:first-child .rm-node:focus-visible ~ .rm-pop { transform: translateX(0) translateY(0); }
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:last-child:hover .rm-pop,
.rm-page .rm-node-wrap:last-child .rm-node:focus-visible ~ .rm-pop { transform: translateX(0) translateY(0); }
.rm-page .rm-pop-title {
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: .07em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 50%, var(--text));
}
.rm-page .rm-pop-goal { font-family: var(--font-serif); font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--text); }
.rm-page .rm-pop-meta { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--text-faint); font-family: var(--font-mono); }
.rm-page .rm-pop-cta {
  font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text-faint);
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: 7px; margin-top: 1px;
}
/* ---------- open / closed ----------
   Gated on html.js-roadmap so the no-JS page keeps every stage visible. */
html.js-roadmap .rm-page .rm-track .rm-stage { display: none; }
html.js-roadmap .rm-page .rm-track .rm-stage.is-open { display: block; animation: rm-open .3s var(--ease); }
html.rm-text-mode .rm-page .rm-track .rm-stage { display: block; }
@keyframes rm-open { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-6px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
html.js-roadmap .rm-page .rm-track .rm-stage.is-open {
  border-left-color: var(--track, var(--accent));
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--track, var(--accent)) 5%, transparent), transparent 40%);
  border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0;
  padding-top: 4px; padding-bottom: 4px;

/* the nudge that tells you the map is clickable, shown only while nothing is */
.rm-page .rm-empty {
  font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--text-faint); font-style: italic;
  padding: 2px 0 6px 22px; margin-bottom: 6px;
}
html.rm-text-mode .rm-page .rm-empty,
.rm-page .rm-track:has(.rm-stage.is-open) .rm-empty { display: none; }
/* ---------- map / full-text switch ---------- */
.rm-modebar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin: 0 0 30px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.rm-modebar-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text-faint); }
.rm-modebar-group { display: inline-flex; background: var(--bg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 999px; padding: 3px; }
.rm-modebar button {
  border: 0; background: none; cursor: pointer; font: inherit;
  font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text-dim);

/* ---------- narrow screens ----------
   The rail goes vertical rather than letting five nodes fight over 360px. */
@media (max-width: 780px) {
  .rm-page .rm-map { flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding: 14px 0 8px; }
  .rm-page .rm-node-wrap + .rm-node-wrap::before {

  .rm-page .rm-hint-tap { display: inline; }
  .rm-page .rm-pop, .rm-page .rm-node-wrap:first-child .rm-pop, .rm-page .rm-node-wrap:last-child .rm-pop {

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {

.rm-page .rm-total {

sampling-lab.html.title: Sampling Lab · KnowML
sampling-lab.html.description: Step through how a next-token distribution becomes an actual token: the softmax and why it subtracts the max, temperature, top-k, top-p/nucleus and the draw itself — every logit, every probability and every count computed live and checkable by hand.

sections.html.title: Browse everything — KnowML
sections.html.description: Every section of KnowML in one place — all 37 topics grouped by theme, the 1950s-to-2026 timeline, the dependency order, and where the scope words actually sit.

tokenizer-lab.html.title: Tokenizer Lab · KnowML
tokenizer-lab.html.description: Train a byte-pair-encoding tokenizer from scratch on a seven-word corpus, one merge at a time — every pair count, every merge, every token computed live — then see exactly why a model that reads tokens cannot count the letters in strawberry.

topics/01-math-foundations.html.title: Math & Stats Foundations · KnowML
topics/01-math-foundations.html.description: Vectors, gradients, Bayes' theorem, cross-entropy, KL divergence, and the bias-variance tradeoff — the small set of math and stats ideas that show up in nearly every ML interview, explained with intuition first.

topics/02-classical-ml.html.description: Linear and logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting and XGBoost, SVMs, k-NN, and naive Bayes — the classical models that still win on tabular data, and what to say about each one in an interview.

topics/03-unsupervised-self-supervised.h.description: Clustering, PCA, autoencoders, and the contrastive and masked-prediction pretext tasks — SimCLR, BERT-style masking — that let a model learn useful structure from data with zero human labels.
